chunks: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Hamid narrated to us; he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us; he said: Ibn Arafah (meaning Al-Hasan) narrated to us; he said: Al-Hakam ibn Zahir narrated to us, from Al-Suddi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit al-Qurashi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said:

A Jew called Bostan al-Yahudi came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad, inform me about the stars that Joseph (peace be upon him) saw prostrating to him, what are their names?' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not answer him at that time about anything. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and informed the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of their names. He said: So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) sent for Bostan, and when he came to him, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked him: 'Will you submit to Islam if I inform you of their names?' He said to him: 'Yes.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jirban, Al-Tariq, Al-Zial, Dhu al-Kanfayn, Qabis, Was'sab, Amoodan, Al-Faylaq, Al-Misbah, Al-Zaruh, Dhu al-Qar', Al-Diya' and Al-Nur. He saw them in the horizon of the sky prostrating to him. When Joseph (peace be upon him) recounted this to Jacob (peace be upon him), Jacob said: 'This is a scattered matter that God, the Exalted, will gather together later.' He said: And Bostan said: 'By God, these are indeed their names.'
ai.seo_question: What are the names of the eleven stars that Joseph saw prostrating to him according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the Prophet’s knowledge of celestial signs as a miracle confirming Joseph’s dream, linking the cosmic order to divine prophecy. The narrative underscores the concept of *I'jaz* (inimitability), where specific astronomical details serve as proof of prophethood, a theme central to Shia exegetical discussions on the unseen (*Ghayb*). It also reflects the historical context of dialogue with Jews in Medina, using shared scriptural knowledge to establish authority.
